how_to_run: The `vectors` section contains endpoint-facing request and expectation pairs: each gives the logical request (payment_intent and optional fields) and what the decision must satisfy; map the request onto your decision endpoint. Expectations use 'decision_at_least' where the rule only raises a decision: review satisfies at_least review, decline satisfies at_least review and decline. Any additional section whose name ends in `_vectors` (for example `origin_binding_vectors` or `continuity_outcome_vectors`) holds deterministic combination vectors: their precomputed check state is test input to the corresponding decision logic, not a field that RAP requires a public decision endpoint to accept.

vectors.name: Payee changed since the previous payment
vectors.why: A clean new address passes every list. Only the change itself shows that the quote may have been altered.

vectors.name: Network changed since the previous payment
vectors.why: The same address string on another chain can be controlled by someone else.

vectors.name: Unchanged payee keeps the screening result
vectors.why: Address case is normalized before comparison. A continuity check that fires on spelling alone trains payers to ignore it.

vectors.name: Token contract set as the payee
vectors.why: Funds sent to a token contract are usually unrecoverable. This is a configuration error, so it is client_error, not regulatory.

vectors.name: Mixer contract as the payee
vectors.why: A decline must come with evidence that names its source.

vectors.name: Invalid intent is rejected, never repaired
vectors.why: Guessing which of two conflicting fields the payer meant produces a decision about a payment nobody intended.

vectors.name: The decision is bound to the intent
vectors.why: The payer computes the digest itself. A decision carrying a different digest was made for a different payment.

vectors.name: Evidence items follow the machine format
vectors.why: Every item states type, subject_ref, source, status and anchor, so a payer's policy can weigh each observation without parsing prose.

origin_binding_vectors.how_to_run: Optional feature: SPEC.md 6.5 (MAY). An implementation that does not implement 6.5 keeps its base RAP conformance without these vectors; an implementation that implements or claims 6.5 MUST pass D9 to D12. To keep the vectors deterministic and isolate the decision-combination semantics, each one supplies the binding outcome as an input rather than depending on a live origin: it gives the decision the service reached before the origin-binding check and the outcome of that check. Feed both into the step of your implementation that combines them, and compare. A raise is a floor: review satisfies at_least review, and so does decline.

vectors.name: Payee bound to the request origin
vectors.why: A bound payee does not change the decision. It shows only that the origin and the payee are consistent, not that the seller is safe.

vectors.name: Payee not bound to the request origin
vectors.why: An applicable check completed and the payee is not bound. An otherwise-allow decision cannot stay allow.

vectors.name: No request origin, check does not apply
vectors.why: A urn: has no HTTP(S) origin, so no binding check applies and the decision is unchanged. not_evaluated is never reported as bound.

vectors.name: Applicable check could not complete
vectors.why: The check applied and did not finish, so it has not passed. An otherwise-allow decision is raised to at least review.
